$comment: Flagged for review. 'needs review' items never block a merge; a broken build does. Each row names the evidence, the owner action that would close it, and whether anything was withheld from the live site as a result.

flags.title: None of the five submitted strings is an ASIN
flags.finding: The brief supplies https://link.amazon/<token> for tokens B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj. Each token is 9 characters. Amazon ASINs are 10 characters. The strings behave as redirector tokens, not identifiers: four of them resolve to listings whose ASINs (B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DZFD6R9Z) share no characters with the submitted token.
flags.consequence: The 'intended ASIN' field is blank for all five rows. A link-level identity claim cannot be made. Anything published against a product uses the observed listing URL only.
flags.owner_action: Paste the ten-character ASINs (or full amazon.com/dp/ URLs) from Associates Central > Links > Special Links, or confirm that 'whatever the short link resolves to today' is the intended target.
flags.discovery_step: In Associates Central, open each product, copy the ASIN from the URL bar, and drop the five ASINs into register/products.json under intended_asin. The build then stops showing the 'identity unconfirmed' state.
flags.withheld_from_site: no product-name or brand claim is attributed to the owner's intent; only observed listing titles are quoted as observations

flags.title: No prices, ratings, review counts, specs or commission rates are published anywhere
flags.finding: Amazon's Program Policies are described (by two secondary sources) as permitting price and availability display only when the data is served by Amazon's own link/widget or pulled from the Creators/PA API, with a 24-hour refresh ceiling. This project holds no API credentials, and the policy text itself was not fetched from the official page (see S02).
flags.consequence: Comparison tables carry criteria, not numbers. The product cards carry a 'what we did not verify' panel instead of a spec sheet. This is the single biggest difference between this site and a typical affiliate site, and it is deliberate.
flags.owner_action: Either (a) keep the no-price stance and lean into 'we tell you how to judge it in 90 seconds' as the brand, or (b) obtain API credentials and let the builder render Amazon-supplied fields with a visible timestamp.
flags.discovery_step: Check Associates Central for a 'Request API access' control and record the eligibility wording you see there; that simultaneously resolves S02, S07 and Q-09.
flags.withheld_from_site: all monetary and rating fields; scripts/checks.mjs fails the build on any currency pattern in docs/

flags.title: Compliance status of the supplied short links is unresolved - not claimed invalid
flags.finding: Section 1 of the Operating Agreement requires links to 'properly use the special tagged link formats we provide'. The four resolved redirect chains ended at amazon.com/dp/ URLs whose recorded final URL carried no tag= parameter. That is an observation about what this environment saw, not proof of what an Associate-created short link transmits: Amazon's own onelink/Associates tooling can attach attribution at a step this fetch could not observe (redirect cookie, session-side tagging, or a later hop).
flags.consequence: The site publishes Special Links built in the documented tagged format with the site's tracking ID, and does not reuse the supplied short links as its primary outbound. The supplied links are not described anywhere on the site as invalid.
flags.owner_action: In Associates Central, generate one Special Links test link per product, click it in a clean browser, and confirm (i) the landing ASIN and (ii) that a session appears in Reports > Transactions. Test one product first, then scale.
flags.discovery_step: One controlled test: new incognito window, click generated link, add any item to cart, do not buy, then read Reports for the session. Record the result in register/links.json test_log.
flags.withheld_from_site: the phrase 'invalid' is never used about the supplied links; the wording used is 'compliance status unresolved'

flags.title: P04 (token B0c8moW59) could not be resolved at all
flags.finding: Three attempts to resolve https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 all landed on an Amazon anti-bot interstitial (amazon.com/checkpoint/continue?token=v1.rJwhW5U-...) rather than a listing. No ASIN, title, brand or category was obtained.
flags.consequence: P04 has no product page on the site and appears in the register as UNRESOLVED. Nothing about it is guessed - not its category, not its brand, not even whether it is a kitchen product.
flags.owner_action: Open the link once in your own browser and paste the resulting amazon.com/dp/ URL, or replace the link.
flags.discovery_step: Resolve manually in a normal browser session (which will not trip the checkpoint), copy the final URL, then re-run npm run build.
flags.withheld_from_site: the product page for P04 and its navigation entry

flags.title: No site URL is registered to the tracking ID, and the site has no analytics deployed
flags.finding: Associates Central requires each Site where Program Content appears to be listed and approved, with the tracking ID attached to it. The Pages URL (https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil3/) is a preview-grade subpath of a github.io domain; it has not been registered and cannot be registered from this environment. The click counter in docs/assets/track.js posts to an endpoint that is implemented locally (scripts/collect.mjs) but not deployed.
flags.consequence: Traffic measurement is currently a stub: events buffer in the reader’s own tab (sessionStorage, cleared when the tab closes) and are transmitted only if a collector endpoint is configured, and monetisation should not be attempted on a github.io subpath.
flags.owner_action: Register a domain you control, point Pages at it, list the exact URL in Associates Central > Account Settings > Site Settings, and create tracking ID shopnow047c-20 if it does not already exist.
flags.discovery_step: Check whether shopnow047c-20 already appears in Account Settings > Tracking IDs. If it does not, create it before publishing any live link.
flags.withheld_from_site: the endpoint URL is left as a documented placeholder rather than pointed at a third-party collector

flags.title: Content is AI-assisted and has had no human editorial sign-off
flags.finding: Every guide on this site was drafted in an automated session. No named human editor reviewed it, and no hands-on testing of any product was performed by this project. The site says so on the methodology page and on each guide.
flags.consequence: The guides are written as *what to look for and what to ask*, never as test results. Words like 'we tested', 'our lab', 'we compared side by side' do not appear, and checks.mjs rejects them.
flags.owner_action: Either adopt the byline as-is (a desk, not a person) or assign a human editor before the site is used for monetised traffic. Do not add a person's name or credentials to 'about' without their agreement.
flags.discovery_step: Answer Q-12 (who signs off) and Q-13 (is a named byline available). Until then the site keeps the disclosure line.
flags.withheld_from_site: no fabricated author biography, no fabricated test data, no invented ratings

flags.title: Repo state did not match the brief's implied history
flags.finding: At base commit 847ae37 the repository contained one file, README.md (8 bytes). The brief refers to an existing 'careful source register', rows SG-27..SG-30, flags FLG-003, and sections S01/S07/S24. No such artifacts exist in any commit on any branch of this repository. Nine sibling session branches exist, each containing only README.md + COORDINATION.md.
flags.consequence: The referenced registers were re-established forward on this branch with the identifiers the brief used, and labelled as newly created rather than recovered. If the real prior work exists in another repository or branch, this site's registers must be reconciled against it before trusting continuity.
flags.owner_action: Point this session at the repository/branch that holds the earlier register if one exists, so the two can be diffed row by row.
flags.discovery_step: git log --all --oneline --name-only on the correct remote; diff the prior register against register/.
flags.withheld_from_site: the site does not claim continuity with an earlier audit; it presents the register it can stand behind

flags.title: Program Policies and API-eligibility pages were not fetched verbatim
flags.finding: Two load-bearing pages resisted in-session retrieval: the Associates Program Policies body (JavaScript console shell) and the USDA FSIS page (fetcher error on 3 attempts, resolved via official-domain excerpt). Where text could not be fetched, this register says so rather than upgrading the claim.
flags.consequence: S02 and S05 carry status 'unresolved' or 'excerpt'. No site copy quotes the price policy's exact wording, and the temperature guide links out to USDA rather than paraphrasing a standard we could not read in full.
flags.owner_action: None required for launch. Optional hardening: re-fetch both from a normal browser and promote the rows to 'verbatim'.
flags.discovery_step: Open each URL, copy the paragraph, paste into register/sources.json under verified_claims, set status verbatim.
flags.withheld_from_site: no verbatim quotation is presented as Amazon policy text where we only had a paraphrase

flags.title: Two parallel sessions claimed the same output paths
flags.finding: Session 772f3220 claimed docs/ and register/ at 05:13Z; this session claimed the same paths at 05:14Z. Because main had no COORDINATION.md, there was no ordering mechanism to arbitrate. No sibling branch contained any site content, so no work was duplicated in a destructive way.
flags.consequence: This branch's docs/ is generated output from its own register/. If another branch is merged afterwards, regenerate docs/ rather than resolving the HTML by hand.
flags.owner_action: Pick one output tree. Recommended: keep the branch whose register is the fuller one (this one has row-level source status), then run npm run build.
flags.discovery_step: git log origin/arena/772f3220-affil3 --stat to compare volume before deciding.

flags.title: No traffic, ranking, revenue or conversion forecast is made anywhere
flags.finding: Section 4 of the Operating Agreement records that Amazon makes no representation about traffic or commission income an Associate can expect. Nothing in this repository measures search demand, and the campaign ledger is empty by design. A revenue model built on those two facts would be invention.
flags.consequence: The site publishes no 'expected earnings', no 'X% conversion rate', no 'this keyword has N volume'. The ledger exists with typed columns and zero rows, and the methodology page explains why.
flags.owner_action: After 2-4 weeks of first-party data, decide whether to fund an SEO tool account; only then does volume-based topic selection become defensible.
flags.discovery_step: Search Console query export (owner action Q-08) is the cheapest first-party substitute for keyword volume and is enough to start.
